summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, chronic abdominal pain, anxiety, and recurrent UTIs was admitted with severe epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had elevated white blood cell count and hyperglycemia on admission. Her pain was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and her home tramadol. A femoral central line was placed due to poor IV access but was removed during the stay due to infection risk. She experienced one episode of hypoglycemia from taking mealtime insulin without eating, which resolved with treatment. Urine culture grew multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, but without signs of active infection, it was not treated. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with instructions to follow up on pending blood cultures and to adjust insulin use when not eating.
